# URLPulse — Full Description

URLPulse is a production-oriented, full-stack application for bulk URL health checking.

## What it does
- Accepts a collection of URLs (manual entry or CSV upload) and groups them into a batch.
- Checks each URL independently as a background job and records the final HTTP status, response time, and page title.
- Streams progress to the browser in real time and reconstructs correct state on refresh.
- Supports batch cancellation and retrying only the failed URLs.

## Architecture (high level)
- Frontend: Next.js (App Router) + React + TypeScript.
- API: Fastify + TypeScript (REST), separate from the worker.
- Worker: a separate process consuming a BullMQ queue backed by Redis.
- Data: PostgreSQL is the authoritative source of truth; Redis provides queueing, coordination, and pub/sub.
- Live updates: Server-Sent Events, treated as notifications only — the database remains authoritative.

## System guarantees
- Global outbound rate limit of 10 requests/second across all workers.
- Global concurrency limit of 5 in-flight checks across all workers.
- Up to 3 retries (4 total attempts) for transient failures, with exponential backoff.
- Idempotent job processing; duplicate delivery cannot corrupt batch state.
- 30-second cache on the batch list with invalidation on relevant mutations.

## Terminology
- "Batch": a submitted group of URLs.
- "URL result": the outcome of checking one URL.
- Statuses: Queued, In Progress, Completed, Failed, Cancelled.

## Public information
- Product name: URLPulse.
- Author: Niranjan Sah.
- Documentation lives under /docs in the repository.
